record.paper_title: Recent Results and Open Problems on the Hydrodynamics of Disordered Asymmetric Exclusion and Zero-Range Processes
record.context_brief: Weak convergence to equilibrium for disordered ZRP
record.original_question: Fix a realization of the site disorder alpha for a disordered zero-range process, and start the process from a spatially ergodic initial distribution of density rho. Let nu^alpha_phi denote the explicit family of invariant product measures for this model, and let rho^* be the critical density when the phase transition occurs. The open question is whether the law of the process eta(t) converges weakly as t tends to infinity to an equilibrium measure nu^alpha_phi determined by the density, and in the phase-transition case with rho > rho^*, whether eta(t) instead converges weakly to the equilibrium state with density rho^*.

evidence.quote: Problem 3. An interesting open problem for the disordered ZRP concerns the weak convergence of the process: Fix the rates α, and take the initial distribution of η(0) spatially ergodic with density ρ. Does the distribution of η(t) converge weakly, as t → ∞, to one of the equilibria ναϕ? If ρ > ρ∗ in the phase transition case, does η(t) converge weakly to the equilibrium with density ρ∗?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the one-dimensional disordered nearest-neighbor zero-range process on $\mathbb{Z}$ defined as follows. The state space is $\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{Z}}$, with configurations $\eta=(\eta(x))_{x\in\mathbb{Z}}$ giving the number of particles at each site. A site-disorder field $\alpha=(\alpha(x))_{x\in\mathbb{Z}}$ is fixed, with $\alpha(x)\in[c,1]$ i.i.d. for some $c>0$. Given a non-decreasing jump-rate function $g:\mathbb{N}\to[0,\infty)$ with $g(0)=0$ and a translation $p(\cdot)$ on $\mathbb{Z}$, the generator acts on local functions by
$$Lf(\eta)=\sum_{x,y}\alpha(x)g(\eta(x))p(y-x)\bigl[f(\eta^{x,y})-f(\eta)\bigr],$$
where $\eta^{x,y}$ denotes the configuration obtained from $\eta$ by moving one particle from $x$ to $y$.

For this model there is an explicit one-parameter family of invariant product measures $\{\nu^{\alpha}_{\varphi}:\varphi\in[0,\varphi_c)\}$, parameterized by a "fugacity" $\varphi$, with mean density 
$$R(\varphi)=\mathbb{E}_{\nu^{\alpha}_{\varphi}}[\eta(0)],$$
which is increasing in $\varphi$. Let $\rho^*=\lim_{\varphi\uparrow\varphi_c}R(\varphi)\in(0,\infty]$ be the critical density (when finite, a condensation phase transition occurs).

Fix the disorder $\alpha$, and assume the process is started from a spatially ergodic initial distribution of density $\rho$, i.e. an ergodic probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ with $\mathbb{E}_{\mu}[\eta(0)]=\rho$. Let $\eta(t)$ denote the resulting Markov process.

Prove or disprove:

(i) If $\rho\le\rho^*$, then the law of $\eta(t)$ converges weakly as $t\to\infty$ to the invariant measure $\nu^{\alpha}_{\varphi}$ with $R(\varphi)=\rho$.

(ii) If $\rho>\rho^*$ (in the phase-transition case where $\rho^*<\infty$), then the law of $\eta(t)$ converges weakly as $t\to\infty$ to the invariant measure with critical density $\rho^*$, namely $\nu^{\alpha}_{\varphi_c^-}$.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has established strong local equilibrium at subcritical and critical hydrodynamic densities, and dynamical loss of mass to the critical equilibrium at supercritical densities, for one-dimensional attractive disordered zero-range processes (Bahadoran–Mountford–Ravishankar–Saada, 2018+). These results are closely related to but weaker than the full weak-convergence statement for arbitrary spatially ergodic initial laws on the whole lattice; a complete proof of weak convergence to $\nu^\alpha_\varphi$ (resp. to the critical measure when $\rho>\rho^*$) starting from a general ergodic measure of density $\rho$ does not appear to be fully established in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Quenched convergence and strong local equilibrium for asymmetric zero-range process with site disorder
status_evidence.snippet: We prove strong local equilibrium at subcritical and critical hydrodynamic densities, and dynamic local loss of mass at supercritical hydrodynamic densities, for the disordered asymmetric zero-range process.
status_evidence.claim: Local equilibrium versions of the conjecture have been proved, but the global weak-convergence statement remains stronger.

status_evidence.title: Zero-Range Process in Random Environment
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of results and remaining open questions for zero-range processes in random environments, including hydrodynamic limits and condensation.
status_evidence.claim: Survey treats the disordered ZRP and indicates that full weak convergence to equilibrium remains a subtle question.
